name: Nineveh
overview: Scripture identifies Nineveh as a prominent city founded by Asshur, situated between Nineveh and Calah, and described as a great city (Genesis 10:11-12). It served as the capital of the Assyrian Empire, where King Sennacherib dwelt after his military campaigns (2 Kings 19:36; Isaiah 37:37). The city’s history includes the violent death of Sennacherib at the hands of his sons while worshiping in the temple of Nisroch, highlighting the divine judgment and turmoil surrounding its rulers (2 Kings 19:37; Isaiah 37:38). These passages underscore Nineveh's significance as a center of power and the backdrop for God’s sovereign intervention in history.
